title: Guru and Education of Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan
summary: The traditional guru lineage and initiation account in the Nimbarka Sampradaya.
body:
Devarshi Shri Narada holds a central place in the guru lineage of the Nimbarka Sampradaya. In the traditional account, Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan appears as an Acharya for the welfare of the world and receives initiation from Narada. The account affirms the importance of the teacher-disciple discipline: even the divine Acharya honours the guru lineage as an example for the world.

## The Kumaras and Narada

The supplied research text cites the passage on Brahma Sutra 1.3.8 in the Vedanta-Parijata-Saurabha, referring to instruction in Brahmavidya from the Kumaras to Narada. It also cites Purushottamacharya's explanation of the sixth verse of the Dashashloki, where 'Shri Naradaya' is explained as 'to our Guru'. These references illuminate the lineage's own scriptural understanding.

## The ideal of discipleship

The supplied edited narrative of *Shri Nimbarka Vikranti* places the meeting with Narada, initiation and the beginning of the digvijaya in sequence. Acceptance of discipleship is presented as an exemplary observance of Vedic discipline and instruction for the world. It teaches that humility and reverence for the Guru must accompany knowledge and spiritual authority.

## Textual verification

A complete treatment requires comparison of the original Vedanta-Parijata-Saurabha, the Dashashloki and the original text attributed to Shri Audumbar Rishi. Where the original text is not available, the edited narrative must be cited with its limitations clearly stated.

Editorial note: This article is based on the supplied research text and edited narrative. Edition and page references of the original works remain to be checked.
